Issue 1 — Cluster 6 has no thumbnails (faces 46, 47)

Both faces survive every quality gate, get assigned to cluster 6, are marked is_core=True, but their crop_path is NaN in faces.csv and no face_0046_* / face_0047_* file exists in crops/. Their embeddings do exist in embeddings.npy, so detection + embedding succeeded — only the crop-persist step skipped them.

Source images (re-detected with InsightFace to recover bboxes)

Bboxes are NOT stored in faces.csv on this run, so we re-ran InsightFace to show what detection actually found. Each rectangle is one detection; the label shows the model's det_score and the raw pixel area.

Comparison: face_26 from a different image, same album, DID get a crop

crop_path=crops/face_0026_aligned.jpg
Same quality flags, same album, same pipeline run.
411/428 faces got a crop; 17 did not.
Verdict — producer bug. The crop stage iterates a different subset than the quality stage. Faces that pass quality and form a real cluster can still be silently dropped before crop persistence. Look at face_cluster/pipeline.py crop stage: which list does it iterate, and what filter is applied between quality-pass and crop-write? Total impact: 17 of 428 faces (4%) on this run.

Issue 2 — face_26 displays as "Area 0 px²"

faces.csv area for face_260.001019 (a fraction)
area column range across all 428 faces min 0.000106, max 0.455136
UI Run-tab control labelmin_face_area px (0=off) — talks pixels
UI Face Analysis tab displayrenders int(area) → "0 px²" for any value <1.0, which is every face on this run

Verdict — column unit drift. The area column is a fraction (0..1). The Run-tab slider, the filter comparison, and the Face Analysis renderer all assume pixels. Need to pick one unit and align all four sites: (a) the column producer in face_cluster/quality.py or face_cluster/pipeline.py, (b) the slider label/range in Run + Recluster tabs, (c) the comparison in the quality gate, (d) the renderer in app/face_clustering/tabs/face_analysis_tab.py. This is a data-contract bug — fixing one site alone makes things worse.

Issue 3 — blur_score = 0 for all faces, det_score = NaN for all faces

The histograms above are degenerate: every face has blur_score = 0.0 exactly, and every face has det_score = NaN. Yet the embeddings are non-zero, so the InsightFace detector ran and returned valid faces.

blur_score: unique values1 (just 0.0)
blur_score: max0.0000
det_score: non-null count0 / 428
quality_blur_value column non-null 428
Verdict — two more producer bugs. Either the blur step never ran, or the export step is overwriting blur_score with a default. det_score is computed by InsightFace itself (it's face.det_score on every detection) but isn't being persisted into faces.csv. Both should be caught by a single export-stage test that asserts no column is uniformly zero/NaN for non-trivial runs.

Issue 3b — merge_log.json missing the four *_pass booleans

The 28-field MergeDecisionRow contract documented in face_cluster/types.py includes support_pass, margin_pass, diameter_pass, distance_pass. None of those exist in the on-disk merge_log on this run, so the FC App's gate badges have to derive pass/fail from the numbers — which is how SIGHTING-058's "Margin: inf" and "4/4 REJECTED" mis-renders appear.

Extra fields on disk that aren't in the expected 28-field contract: exemplar_dist, margin_competitor_dist, margin_competitor_id, margin_dist_to_b, passes_cross, passes_diameter, passes_exemplar, passes_margin, passes_support, threshold_used

Verdict — schema mismatch in the legacy writer. Phase 1 of spec-030 added a v4 layout under _v4/ that does include all 28 fields in the DB merge_decisions table — but the legacy merge_log.json writer next to it still emits the lossy old shape, and FC App on main reads the legacy file. Fixing requires either (a) cutting FC App over to RunStore (Phase 3 — branch spec-030-phase-3-ui-cutover, not yet merged), or (b) backporting the missing fields into the legacy writer.

Issue 5 — Cluster 4 is a chain merge (n=28 faces)

You said the merge distances looked fake. They aren't — the per-pair distances are real. The problem is that cluster 4 itself, before any merge gate runs, already contains multiple identities chain-linked together.

n faces in cluster 428
internal cosine distance: min / mean / max 0.115 / 0.471 / 0.867
DBSCAN sub-clusters at eps=0.32 3 sub-clusters + 6 noise

Anything above ~0.40 cosine distance between two ArcFace embeddings is "different person" territory. Cluster 4 has internal max 0.867, which means at least one pair inside this single cluster is essentially unrelated.

Pairwise distance heatmap (rows/cols ordered by hierarchical clustering)

Look for the dark-blue blocks along the diagonal — each block is a genuinely-similar sub-group. The bright off-diagonal cells are pairs of "different people" that ended up in the same cluster because base clustering's mutual-kNN graph chained them through intermediate faces.

DBSCAN sub-clustering of cluster 4 (eps=0.32, ArcFace cosine)

Sub-cluster 0 (n=17)

Sub-cluster 1 (n=3)

Sub-cluster 2 (n=2)

DBSCAN noise (n=6)

Verdict — algorithm tuning, not a data bug. The base mutual-kNN clustering at distance_threshold=0.35, K=5 is too permissive for this album. DBSCAN at the same data finds 3 natural sub-groups inside what the pipeline called a single cluster. Wait until you compare to the standalone-app "satisfactory" run before changing anything — the gap between this run's params and that run's params is the most useful diagnostic we have.

Where to go from here

  1. Producer bugs (Issues 1, 2, 3a, 3b, 3c) need separate small fixes, each with a regression test. None depend on spec-030 Phase 3 landing.
  2. Schema-mismatch in merge_log.json (Issue 3b) resolves automatically if Phase 3 is merged to main and Phase 4 deletes the legacy writer. That branch (spec-030-phase-3-ui-cutover) is ready.
  3. Cluster 4 chain (Issue 5) is parked until the user provides their "satisfactory" standalone run for parameter comparison.
